title: Brake Noise and Squeal Service After a Brake Job
content:
**Q. When is brake noise serviced free under Brake Service Warranties?**
A squeal or grinding noise soon after a brake job is serviced free when it is confirmed at inspection as a noise squeal. A noise service means the pads are cleaned and the shims and lubrication renewed. The noise service must be performed no later than the end of the noise service period counted from the original brake job. The period is the line's noise service days, and the number of noise services already recorded under this warranty must be below the line's free noise services per warranty. After either limit the service is charged at the line's pad replacement labor price per axle.

**Q. How is the period counted?**
In calendar days, counted from the day after the anchor date — the date of the original brake job — so the anchor date plus the number of days is the last qualifying date. A noise service on that last date is within the period; one on the next day is not.

*Illustration (illustrative 20-day period, not any line's figure).* For a job dated the 5th of a month, day 1 is the 6th and day 20 is the 25th: a noise service on the 25th qualifies, one on the 26th does not.

**Q. What if the period has run out, or the free services are used up?**

| Within the noise service period | Noise services already recorded below the line's free number | Noise service |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | free |
| Yes | No | charged at the line's pad replacement labor price per axle |
| No | Yes | charged at the line's pad replacement labor price per axle |
| No | No | charged at the line's pad replacement labor price per axle |

**Q. Is every noise a noise service?**
No. Noise from worn pads, a seized caliper or contamination is not a noise service and follows its own finding.

**Q. Whose noise services count?**
Only those recorded under this warranty, over its whole life; each brake job on each axle keeps its own count.
